kind: literature / source audit for the O/O2 electron-impact reaction set (no implementation)
compiled_by: source-audit lane D (agent session); not reviewed by the project owner
authority: None. This file records which published sources exist, how they can be accessed and what they cover. It builds no rate table, changes no chemistry, threshold, solver setting or frozen dataset, and is not a pre-registration. Status values here say whether a source was found, not that a process is included, promoted or validated.
gating: CLAUDE.md 'Next work' item 4: O2/O chemistry is taken up only if items 1-3 succeed. The draft completeness rule (o_o2_completeness_prereg_DRAFT.json, same folder) must be frozen by the owner before any O/O2 rate table is built or any O/O2 reaction enters a propellant configuration.

scope.why: Atmospheric (VLEO, 180-230 km per the RFP envelope in CLAUDE.md) Hall operation ingests atomic O together with N2 and O2 after the intake/compressor path. Species fractions are not stated here; they come from the frozen atmosphere + intake model and are outside this audit.
excluded: heavy-particle chemistry (charge exchange, ion-molecule reactions such as O+ + N2, NO formation): not electron-impact; not surveyed in this lane
surface processes (wall recombination of O in the intake, compressor or channel): outside the ionization/discharge block and outside this audit

policy.lxcat: NOT USED. No LXCat page, database or download was accessed for this audit, and no row relies on an LXCat-distributed dataset (see source ALVES2016 note). Same position as hallthruster_bridge/propellants/PROVENANCE.md (2026-09-25).
policy.published_sources_only: Only published, openly listed sources are recorded. No person or laboratory was contacted. Private communications cited by reviews are flagged as not usable (source BG_OP).
policy.access: Paywalled full texts were not accessed. Two pages returned HTTP 403 to automated fetches (the AIP article page of SONG2026 and the UCL Discovery record page); these were not bypassed. No TLS or trust setting was changed.
policy.verification: A source is listed only if its existence was confirmed from at least one of: Crossref metadata (api.crossref.org), a publisher/arXiv/OSTI/PubMed record returned by search, or a document actually downloaded and read (sha256 recorded). Items whose bibliographic detail was taken only from a reference list are marked 'citation per <list>; DOI not verified'.
policy.numbers: Every number in this file is quoted from the named source with the source's own wording where possible. Nothing is fitted, derived or interpolated here. Values read from a PDF text layer (not the page image) are marked 'text layer; verify against page image'. SONG2026 values were read from the accepted manuscript; they must be checked against the version of record or its supplementary data before any table is built.

status.source-identified: At least one verified published source gives the needed quantity for this process over its main energy range. Remaining choices are recorded in open_issues.
status.source-open: Sources exist, but a substantive owner decision is needed before a table could be built: evaluators could not recommend values, sources conflict without resolution, the recommended data stop inside the physically relevant range, the process is model-only, or two candidate processes overlap (double counting).
status.gap: No usable published source was located in this audit for the needed quantity (which may simply mean it was not surveyed; the row says which).

access.open: The numeric content needed is readable without subscription (open reprint, arXiv, NIST, open accepted manuscript) and was accessed.
access.paywalled: The primary text is behind a subscription and was not accessed; only metadata/abstract were seen.
access.mixed: The recommended source is paywalled or its numeric supplement was not accessed, but an open route to the recommendation or to an alternative exists (stated in access_detail).
access.not-verified: Access could not be determined without bypassing a block or was not attempted.
access.none: No source, so no access route.

vocabulary.evidence_level: docs/EVIDENCE.md hierarchy (1 = in-house hardware ... 4 = validated physics or evaluated-data literature, 5 = indirect/secondary, 6 = extrapolation, 7 = assumption). Recorded per source.
vocabulary.quantity_type: docs/EVIDENCE.md: measured / digitized / inferred / reconstructed / model-derived / assumed. Recorded per candidate-source entry.

SONG2026.citation: M.-Y. Song, H. Cho, G. P. Karwasz, V. Kokoouline, J. Tennyson and K. Bartschat, 'Cross Sections for Electron Collisions with Molecular and Atomic Oxygen', J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 55, 013102 (2026)
SONG2026.verified_by: Crossref metadata (journal, volume 55, issue 1, article 013102, published 2026-03-01 print / 2026-03-02 online); accepted manuscript downloaded and read in full
SONG2026.document_version: accepted manuscript, 'Revised 26 November 2025' (22 pages); version of record not accessed (AIP page returned HTTP 403 to fetch); licence of the manuscript copy not verified (UCL record page returned HTTP 403)
SONG2026.access_detail: Accepted manuscript open on UCL Discovery; version of record at AIP not accessed; the recommended datasets are provided as supplementary material (Data Availability section), which was not accessed.
SONG2026.role: Primary recommended compilation for both O2 and O (literature to end of 2024). The direct analogue of Song et al. JPCRD 52, 023104 (2023) used for N2.
known_manuscript_issues: Table V (O2 MTCS) has a row '0.008 eV | 2.30' between 0.060 and 0.090 eV, apparently 0.080 eV; verify against the version of record.
Reference 10 (Itikawa, JPCRD 38, 1) is dated 2008 in the manuscript; the NIST-hosted reprints of other Itikawa papers cite it as 2009, and Crossref lists 'issued' 2008. Bibliographic detail only.
Section F text writes the Schumann-Runge upper state as 'b3Sigma_u-' in the text layer; conventionally B3Sigma_u-. Verify against the version of record.

Fig. 25 (atomic O, optically allowed): the caption names the lower panel (2p3 3s) 3D while the in-plot label reads (2p3 3d) 3D. Which transition is shown must be verified against the version of record.

ITIKAWA2009.citation: Y. Itikawa, 'Cross Sections for Electron Collisions with Oxygen Molecules', J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 38, 1-20 (2009)
ITIKAWA2009.access_detail: No NIST-hosted reprint found (https://srd.nist.gov/jpcrdreprint/1.3025886.pdf returned HTTP 404). AIP copy not accessed.
ITIKAWA2009.role: Previous O2 recommendation (literature to end of 2007). Superseded by SONG2026 for most processes; cross-check only.

ITIKAWA1989.citation: Y. Itikawa, A. Ichimura, K. Onda, K. Sakimoto, K. Takayanagi, Y. Hatano, M. Hayashi, H. Nishimura and S. Tsurubuchi, 'Cross Sections for Collisions of Electrons and Photons with Oxygen Molecules', J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 18, 23-42 (1989)
ITIKAWA1989.verified_by: Crossref metadata; NIST-hosted reprint downloaded (first page read)

II1990.citation: Y. Itikawa and A. Ichimura, 'Cross Sections for Collisions of Electrons and Photons with Atomic Oxygen', J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 19, 637-651 (1990)
II1990.verified_by: Crossref metadata; NIST-hosted reprint downloaded and sections 4, 5.1 and 7 read
II1990.role: Older atomic-O compilation: elastic and momentum transfer (Sec. 4.1: only one Q_m source, Thomas & Nesbet), fine-structure transitions of the ground term (Sec. 5.1, from Berrington's R-matrix collision strengths), radiative and three-body attachment to O (Sec. 7).

LG1990.citation: R. R. Laher and F. R. Gilmore, 'Updated Excitation and Ionization Cross Sections for Electron Impact on Atomic Oxygen', J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 19, 277-305 (1990)
LG1990.verified_by: NIST-hosted reprint downloaded (abstract and contents read); ADS record 1990JPCRD..19..277L (search result)
LG1990.role: Critical review of O excitation (more than 60 profiles: the metastable 2p4 1D and 1S, the autoionizing 2p5 3P, nine allowed and twenty-nine forbidden Rydberg series) and ionization to O+(4S, 2D, 2P), inner-shell O+(4P) and O^2+ (abstract). Open alternative/cross-check to TZ2016.
LG1990.note: A DTIC report version exists (https://apps.dtic.mil/sti/tr/pdf/ADA206987.pdf per search) but returned HTTP 403 and was not accessed.

BELL1983.citation: K. L. Bell, H. B. Gilbody, J. G. Hughes, A. E. Kingston and F. J. Smith, 'Recommended Data on the Electron Impact Ionization of Light Atoms and Ions', J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 12, 891-916 (1983)
BELL1983.verified_by: Crossref metadata; NIST-hosted reprint downloaded (sha256 identical to the copy recorded in scripts/build_n_z1plus_to_z2plus_table.py); Table 5 and Sec. 4.8 read from the text layer
BELL1983.role: Recommended Eq. (1) fits for O I, O II (O+ -> O^2+), O III (O^2+ -> O^3+). Table 5 reliability at 67 % confidence.

AH1971.citation: K. L. Aitken and M. F. A. Harrison, 'Measurement of the cross sections for electron impact ionization of multi-electron ions; I. O+ to O2+ and O2+ to O3+', J. Phys. B 4, 1176-1188 (1971)
AH1971.role: Crossed-beam measurement underlying the BELL1983 O II recommendation; BELL1983 Sec. 4.8 notes 2P and 2D metastable ions in the O+ beam.

NIST107_O.citation: NIST Standard Reference Database 107 (Electron-Impact Cross Sections for Ionization and Excitation), atomic O table: BEB direct + excitation-autoionization of Kim & Desclaux 2002, with experimental points of Brook et al. 1978 (2 kV and 4 kV), Thompson et al. 1995 and Zipf 1985
NIST107_O.role: Open numeric route to the BEB ionization cross section of O(3P) and to the THOMPSON1995 points (same access pattern as ionization_N.dat; the NIST table itself is not committed).
NIST107_O.coverage_as_fetched: BEB total: 129 energies, 13.62-5000 eV; Thompson 1995: 47 points, 14.1-2000 eV; Brook 1978 2 kV: 21 points, 14.7-397 eV; Brook 1978 4 kV: 10 points, 47-997 eV; Zipf 1985: 16 points, 40-300 eV (counts from our parse of the fetched table).

NIST107_O2.citation: NIST Standard Reference Database 107, O2 molecule entry: BEB orbital constants and cross section, reference W. Hwang, Y.-K. Kim and M. E. Rudd, J. Chem. Phys. 104, 2956-2966 (1996)
NIST107_O2.verified_by: molecule index and O2 page fetched 2026-09-26 (orbital constants table read; cross-section table not downloaded). Hwang et al. citation as printed by NIST; DOI not verified (Crossref lookup rate-limited).
NIST107_O2.role: Model cross-check for total (counting) O2 ionization only; BEB does not partition O2+ / O+ / O^2+.

KD2002.citation: Y.-K. Kim and J.-P. Desclaux, 'Ionization of carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen by electron impact', Phys. Rev. A 66, 012708 (2002)
KD2002.role: BEB theory behind NIST107_O (already used for N in ionization_N.dat).

THOMPSON1995.citation: W. R. Thompson, M. B. Shah and H. B. Gilbody, 'Single and double ionization of atomic oxygen by electron impact', J. Phys. B 28, 1321-1330 (1995)
THOMPSON1995.verified_by: Crossref metadata; data points tabulated in NIST107_O
THOMPSON1995.role: Recommended O ionization by SONG2026 ('most recent experimental data ... agree very well with the BEB predictions'); also measures double ionization of O.

BROOK1978.citation: E. Brook, M. F. A. Harrison and A. C. H. Smith, 'Measurements of the electron impact ionisation cross sections of He, C, O and N atoms', J. Phys. B 11, 3115-3132 (1978)
BROOK1978.verified_by: Crossref metadata; points tabulated in NIST107_O
BROOK1978.role: Earlier O ionization measurement; SONG2026 notes an ion signal already at 12.9 eV (below the 13.62 eV threshold) and the possibility of ionization from metastable 1D.

TZ2016.citation: S. S. Tayal and O. Zatsarinny, 'B-spline R-matrix-with-pseudostates approach for excitation and ionization of atomic oxygen by electron collisions', Phys. Rev. A 94, 042707 (2016)
TZ2016.verified_by: Crossref metadata (APS default licence and APS accepted-manuscript licence listed); APS abstract returned by search
TZ2016.access_detail: APS article paywalled; the APS accepted-manuscript link (https://link.aps.org/accepted/10.1103/PhysRevA.94.042707) returned HTTP 403 and was not bypassed; access to its supplemental data file not verified. SONG2026's own supplementary material (not accessed) is the other route to the BSR-1116 numbers it recommends.
TZ2016.role: BSR-1116 model (19 spectroscopic bound states + 1097 pseudo-states, per SONG2026). SONG2026 recommends it for O elastic, momentum transfer and all excitation cross sections, 'on a narrow energy grid between the respective thresholds and 200 eV'; also gives ionization of O(3P) and O(1D).

WA1989.citation: J. F. Williams and L. J. Allen, 'Low-energy elastic scattering of electrons from atomic oxygen', J. Phys. B 22, 3529-3539 (1989)
WA1989.role: Only elastic DCS measurement for O used by SONG2026 (five energies); experimental cross-check for the O MTCS.

BG_OP.citation: F. Blanco and G. Garcia, optical-potential (OP) calculation for e-O, cited by SONG2026 as 'private communication (2025)', method described in K. R. Hamilton et al., J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 50, 013101 (2021)
BG_OP.role: Proposed by SONG2026 as an alternative for O cross sections at and above 200 eV. As a private communication it is NOT usable under the project's published-sources rule unless the numbers are published (e.g. in SONG2026's supplementary material, then as a secondary model-derived source).

HMS2017.citation: M. Hahn, A. Mueller and D. W. Savin, 'Electron-impact Multiple-ionization Cross Sections for Atoms and Ions of Helium through Zinc', Astrophys. J. 850, 122 (2017)
HMS2017.verified_by: Crossref metadata; already used for N in hallthruster_bridge/propellants/PROVENANCE.md (arXiv:1708.02155, VizieR J/ApJ/850/122)
HMS2017.access_detail: Open via arXiv:1708.02155 and VizieR (as recorded in PROVENANCE.md; not re-fetched in this audit).
HMS2017.role: Semi-empirical direct double ionization. PROVENANCE.md records HMS Sec. 3.7: the scheme overestimates neutral O by about a factor 2, so for O it is a bound, not a nominal.

LM2003.citation: B. G. Lindsay and M. A. Mangan, '5.1 Ionization', Landolt-Boernstein Group I Vol. 17C, Interactions of Photons and Electrons with Molecules (Springer, 2003)
LM2003.verified_by: citation per SONG2026 reference 17; DOI not verified
LM2003.role: Evaluation behind SONG2026 Table VII (O2 total and partial ionization), based on STRAUB1996 renormalized.

STRAUB1996.citation: H. C. Straub, P. Renault, B. G. Lindsay, K. A. Smith and R. F. Stebbings, 'Absolute partial cross sections for electron-impact ionization of H2, N2, and O2 from threshold to 1000 eV', Phys. Rev. A 54, 2146-2153 (1996)
STRAUB1996.role: Measured partial O2 ionization (O2+, O+, O^2+) underlying LM2003 / SONG2026 Table VII.

TV1998.citation: C. Tian and C. R. Vidal, 'Electron impact ionization of N2 and O2: contributions from different dissociation channels of multiply ionized molecules', J. Phys. B 31, 5369-5381 (1998)
TV1998.role: Channel-resolved O+ production: single (O+ + O) versus double (O+ + O+) ionization (plotted as lines in SONG2026 Fig. 16).

MARK1975.citation: T. D. Maerk, 'Cross section for single and double ionization of N2 and O2 molecules by electron impact from threshold up to 170 eV', J. Chem. Phys. 63, 3731-3736 (1975)
MARK1975.role: Early separate O2^2+ yield (on 17O16O, per SONG2026).

SIGAUD2013.citation: L. Sigaud, N. Ferreira and E. C. Montenegro, 'Absolute cross sections for O2 dication production by electron impact', J. Chem. Phys. 139, 024302 (2013)

BULL2015.citation: J. N. Bull, J. W. L. Lee and C. Vallance, 'Electron ionization dynamics of N2 and O2 molecules: Velocity-map imaging', Phys. Rev. A 91, 022704 (2015)
BULL2015.role: O2^2+ yield (about 10 % of the O+ signal at 100 eV, per SONG2026) and O+ product-state distribution.

JIA2023.citation: S. Jia et al., 'Cold-target electron-ion-coincidence momentum-spectroscopy study of electron-impact single and double ionization of N2 and O2 molecules', Phys. Rev. A 107, 032819 (2023)
JIA2023.role: O2^2+ yield by TOF and position-sensitive methods (SONG2026 Fig. 17).

RE1965.citation: D. Rapp and P. Englander-Golden, 'Total Cross Sections for Ionization and Attachment in Gases by Electron Impact. I. Positive Ionization', J. Chem. Phys. 43, 1464-1479 (1965)

COSBY1993.citation: P. C. Cosby, 'Electron-impact dissociation of oxygen', J. Chem. Phys. 98, 9560-9569 (1993)
COSBY1993.role: Measured total dissociation of O2 into neutrals; SONG2026 Table VI (companion of the N2 paper used for dissociation_N2.dat).

LECLAIR1993.citation: L. R. LeClair and J. W. McConkey, 'Selective detection of O(1S) following electron impact dissociation of O2 and N2O using a XeO* conversion technique', J. Chem. Phys. 99, 4566-4577 (1993)
LECLAIR1993.role: O(1S) fragment production (a factor 50 below COSBY1993's total, per SONG2026).

LAPORTA2013.citation: V. Laporta, R. Celiberto and J. Tennyson, 'Resonant vibrational-excitation cross sections and rate constants for low-energy electron scattering by molecular oxygen', Plasma Sources Sci. Technol. 22, 025001 (2013)
LAPORTA2013.verified_by: Crossref metadata; arXiv:1604.05871 record and PDF downloaded and scanned
LAPORTA2013.access_detail: Preprint open on arXiv (licence nonexclusive-distrib/1.0: read, not redistribute). The numeric cross sections are 'made available for use by modelers' as supplementary material of the journal article; that supplement was not accessed.
LAPORTA2013.role: Recommended O2 vibrational excitation (SONG2026): all 42 vibrational levels, four O2- resonances (2Pi_g, 2Pi_u, 4Sigma_u-, 2Sigma_u-), R-matrix + boomerang model, rotation J = 1-151.

ALTHOUFEK2021.citation: V. Alt and K. Houfek, 'Resonant collisions of electrons with O2 via the lowest-lying 2Pi_g state of O2-', Phys. Rev. A 103, 032829 (2021)
ALTHOUFEK2021.verified_by: PDF downloaded from the authors' institute site (journal header read); DOI as printed, Crossref not queried
ALTHOUFEK2021.role: Alternative O2 vibrational excitation (nonlocal resonance model, v = 0 -> 1-7). SONG2026: cross sections for certain transitions differ from LAPORTA2013 'by as much as a factor of 4'; LAPORTA2013 agrees better with measurements.

GS1955.citation: E. Gerjuoy and S. Stein, 'Rotational Excitation by Slow Electrons', Phys. Rev. 97, 1671-1679 (1955)
GS1955.role: Born-approximation quadrupole rotational excitation formula quoted in SONG2026 Eq. (1) (the formula itself is open in the SONG2026 manuscript).

HUANG2022.citation: C. Huang, H. Zhang and X. Cheng, 'R-Matrix Calculation of Electron Collisions with Molecular Oxygen in Its Electronically Excited States', J. Phys. Chem. A 126, 2061-2074 (2022)
HUANG2022.role: Recommended O2 electronic excitation (SONG2026): fixed-nuclei R-matrix, ground and excited initial states; per the abstract returned by search it reports (de-)excitation for the Herzberg states and the B3Sigma_u- state.

TASHIRO2006.citation: M. Tashiro, K. Morokuma and J. Tennyson, 'R-matrix calculation of electron collisions with electronically excited O2 molecules', Phys. Rev. A 73, 052707 (2006)
TASHIRO2006.role: Earlier R-matrix set, close to HUANG2022 (SONG2026); open alternative; source of SONG2026 Fig. 12 (b1Sigma_g+ initial state).

SHYN1993.citation: T. W. Shyn and C. J. Sweeney, 'Differential electronic-excitation cross sections of molecular oxygen by electron impact: The a1Delta_g and b1Sigma_g+ states', Phys. Rev. A 47, 1006 (1993)
SHYN1993.verified_by: citation per SONG2026 reference 75; DOI not verified
SHYN1993.role: Measured a and b excitation; the previous recommendation (ITIKAWA2009 via SONG2026).

SHYN1994.citation: T. W. Shyn, C. J. Sweeney, A. Grafe and W. E. Sharp, 'Absolute differential cross sections for the excitation of molecular oxygen by electron impact: Decomposition of the Schumann-Runge continuum', Phys. Rev. A 50, 4794 (1994)
SHYN1994.verified_by: citation per SONG2026 reference 77; DOI not verified
SHYN1994.role: Measured Schumann-Runge-region excitation; ITIKAWA2009 did not recommend such data 'due to the large uncertainty' (SONG2026).

TB1989.citation: D. Teillet-Billy, L. Malegat, J. P. Gauyacq, R. Abouaf and C. Benoit, 'Electronic excitation to the O2 (... pi_u^3 pi_g^3) states in e-O2 collisions', J. Phys. B 22, 1095 (1989)
TB1989.verified_by: citation per SONG2026 reference 86; DOI not verified
TB1989.role: Measured sum of the three Herzberg-state excitations (SONG2026 Fig. 10).

RB1965.citation: D. Rapp and D. D. Briglia, 'Total Cross Sections for Ionization and Attachment in Gases by Electron Impact. II. Negative-Ion Formation', J. Chem. Phys. 43, 1480-1489 (1965)
RB1965.role: Dissociative electron attachment of O2, recommended by SONG2026 Table VIII (and by the previous reviews).

CHRISTOPHOROU1965.citation: L. G. Christophorou, R. N. Compton, G. S. Hurst and P. W. Reinhardt, 'Determination of Electron-Capture Cross Sections with Swarm-Beam Techniques', J. Chem. Phys. 43, 4273-4281 (1965)
CHRISTOPHOROU1965.role: Swarm-beam DEA of O2, in agreement with RB1965 (SONG2026).

LAPORTA2015.citation: V. Laporta, R. Celiberto and J. Tennyson, 'Dissociative electron attachment and electron-impact resonant dissociation of vibrationally excited O2 molecules', Phys. Rev. A 91, 012701 (2015)
LAPORTA2015.verified_by: arXiv:1501.01771 record (journal reference and DOI listed there)
LAPORTA2015.role: Vibrational-state-resolved DEA and resonant dissociation. Note: the arXiv abstract says the main v = 0 contribution is the 2Pi_u resonance with a significant 4Sigma contribution, whereas the SONG2026 manuscript text says DEA from low v 'largely goes via the 4Sigma_u- resonance'; recorded, not resolved.

CH2006.citation: S. Cherkani-Hassani, D. S. Belic, J. J. Jureta and P. Defrance, 'Absolute cross sections for electron impact ionization and dissociation of O2+', J. Phys. B 39, 5105-5117 (2006)
CH2006.verified_by: Crossref metadata (authors, pages); abstract as returned by search (IOPscience / OSTI ETDEWEB 20907331 records)
CH2006.role: Crossed-beam O2+ single ionization (O2+ -> O2^2+), dissociative ionization and dissociative excitation, threshold to about 2.5 keV. Abstract maxima: (2.20 +/- 0.09) x 1e-17 cm^2 simple ionization, (5.3 +/- 1.0) x 1e-17 cm^2 dissociative ionization, (22.0 +/- 4.6) x 1e-17 cm^2 dissociative excitation; fragment kinetic energy release up to about 20 eV.

VK1996.citation: L. Vejby-Christensen, D. Kella, D. Mathur, H. B. Pedersen, H. T. Schmidt and L. H. Andersen, 'Electron-impact detachment from negative ions', Phys. Rev. A 53, 2371-2378 (1996)
VK1996.verified_by: Crossref metadata; OSTI record 279920 summary returned by search (D- and O-, threshold to about 30 eV)
VK1996.role: Electron-impact detachment of O- (e + O- -> O + 2e).

PEVERALL2001.citation: R. Peverall et al., 'Dissociative recombination and excitation of O2+: Cross sections, product yields and implications for studies of ionospheric airglows', J. Chem. Phys. 114, 6679-6689 (2001)
PEVERALL2001.role: Storage-ring DR and dissociative excitation cross sections of O2+.

FMM2006.citation: A. I. Florescu-Mitchell and J. B. A. Mitchell, 'Dissociative recombination', Phys. Rep. 430, 277-374 (2006)

ANZAI2012.citation: K. Anzai et al., 'Cross section data sets for electron collisions with H2, O2, CO, CO2, N2O and H2O', Eur. Phys. J. D 66, 36 (2012)
ANZAI2012.role: Earlier multi-molecule compilation; secondary cross-check only.

ALVES2016.citation: L. L. Alves, P. Coche, M. A. Ridenti and V. Guerra, 'Electron scattering cross sections for the modelling of oxygen-containing plasmas', Eur. Phys. J. D 70, 124 (2016)
ALVES2016.role: Context only. Its numeric cross-section set is distributed through LXCat, so it is not used as a data source here (project policy).

JEON2003.citation: B.-H. Jeon, 'Determination of electron collision cross-sections for the oxygen molecule by using an electron swarm study', J. Korean Phys. Soc. 43, 513-525 (2003)
JEON2003.verified_by: citation per SONG2026 reference 45; DOI not verified (Crossref lookup rate-limited)
JEON2003.role: Swarm-derived O2 MTCS used by SONG2026 from 0.001 to 0.8 eV (no uncertainties given by Jeon).

TANAKA2016.citation: H. Tanaka, M. J. Brunger, L. Campbell, H. Kato, M. Hoshino and A. Rau, 'Scaled plane-wave Born cross sections for atoms and molecules', Rev. Mod. Phys. 88, 025004 (2016)
TANAKA2016.verified_by: citation per SONG2026 reference 46; DOI not verified
TANAKA2016.role: Candidate route for high-energy extension of electronic excitation (scaled Born); SONG2026 says it repeated the ITIKAWA2009 electronic-excitation recommendations. Not evaluated here.

context_only_sources.ALVES2016: context only; numeric set distributed via LXCat, not used

cross_cutting_findings.finding: A new evaluated compilation exists for both O2 and O: SONG2026 (JPCRD 55, 013102, 2026), from the same group whose 2023 N2 review underlies most of abep-n2n. Its accepted manuscript is open; its version of record and supplementary datasets were not accessed. Every transcription must be checked against the version of record or the supplement (known manuscript issues are listed under the source).

Negative ions in the installed solver. The locally installed HallThruster package source (~/.julia/packages/HallThruster/zHCae, Project.toml version 0.23.1) contains negative-ion handling: src/simulation/heavy_species_update.jl defines _K_MUTUAL_NEUTRALIZATION = 1.0e-12 m^3/s (comment: 'lit. ~4e-14 to ~1e-12') and _K_NEUTRAL_DETACHMENT = 1.0e-12 m^3/s, applied to any fluid with Z < 0, plus an electronegative Bohm correction citing 'Ridenti et al (2025) Eq. (18)'. These constants carry no citation in the code and are species-independent. If O- were ever modelled, they would enter silently, which conflicts with CLAUDE.md rules 3 (no silent fallbacks) and 6 (cite data). Whether this installed tree is byte-identical to the pinned commit bfb3019 (hallthruster_bridge/Manifest.toml git-tree-sha1 7505b3a2...) was not checked in this audit (verify). No Julia was run.

Documented reaction types of the pinned solver (docs/src/howto/new_propellant.md in the installed package): elastic/momentum transfer, excitation, and electron-impact reactions (dissociation, ionization, dissociative ionization). Attachment, detachment and recombination are not documented. Rows OO2-16 and OO2-21..24 therefore also carry an implementability question, separate from source availability.

O2 dissociation versus electronic excitation double counting (OO2-08, OO2-11, OO2-12): the recommended total dissociation (Cosby) starts at 13.5 eV while the dissociative Herzberg and Schumann-Runge excitations lie below it, and above 13.5 eV both count the same events. N2 did not force this choice as sharply. An owner decision on the accounting must precede any table.

Recommended O data (BSR-1116) end at 200 eV and the SONG2026-suggested high-energy continuation (BG_OP) is a private communication. Because HallThruster tables run to 255 eV mean energy, the rate share beyond the last cited point must be computed and a validity limit set in rate_validity.toml style before any O table is called verified.

The 0-D chemistry (abep_sim/plasma_chem.py) uses unverified Arrhenius fits for O and O2 ionization, O2 dissociative ionization and O2 dissociation (CLAUDE.md next-work 6). The rows note which source would replace each entry. Nothing in abep_sim was modified; wiring any table into plasma_chem would be a model change (goldens move, log it).

No published O2/air Hall-thruster validation measurements were surveyed in this lane. Any O/O2 validation target is TBD and requires its own measurement audit and pre-registration (the P5-N2 workflow), after the chemistry rule is frozen.
